tasks.task: Write a brand voice guide from the client's own writing

items.when: When the client has writing they like and needs a short guide the whole team can follow
Before you start, to find the style guides, decks and call notes the client already has
When the best source is documents or call transcripts and you need rules with examples
When you want a one-page version with tone sliders and word lists to compare with the full guide
When the client wants the guide, new copy in that voice and a check in one run
When the guide is drafted, to run real drafts through it and see if it catches what it should
When the guide is all adjectives and should say what to cut and what to keep in a sentence

tasks.task: Check draft copy against the voice guide

items.when: When you have draft copy and the client's voice guide and messaging to check it against
When you want each deviation ranked by how serious it is
When the draft came from an AI tool and reads like one
When the check fails and the copy must be rewritten in the brand's voice

tasks.task: Check the message is the same across touchpoints

items.when: When site, emails, packaging and ads must be read against one voice and one message
When the touchpoints disagree and each needs bringing into line
When the client is a store and you want a score for what each touchpoint says

tasks.task: Build a brand fact file any writer or AI tool can use

items.when: When the client wants one file: who they are, what they sell, to whom, what they may claim
When the website is the best source and a founder interview must fill its gaps
When facts are missing and you need a ranked list of questions for the founder
When colours, fonts, voice and dated prices must be measured from the live site
When the file is agreed and the client wants a printable guide and a values file for AI tools
Before the file is shared, to check every claim it says writers may make
When you have interviews, surveys or tickets and need patterns and the words buyers use
When interviews are still to run and draft questions lead the witness
When orders and reviews exist and you need a buyer profile built on the job they hire for
When you know little yet and need who it is for, who the rivals are and where it could stand

tasks.task: Map what every rival already says

items.when: Before positioning, naming or a tagline, to see what rivals say so you stop saying the same
When you need rivals' messages and positioning side by side with the gaps
When you need the word each rival owns and the words nobody can claim
When you want a grid of what buyers value against who is strong, to find open ground
When the client wants to say what the leader says, only louder
When you have buyer evidence and rival messages and need a position and the reasons for it
When a new business or a reset needs position, name and voice decided in order
When you need several ways to stand apart, each with a statement, before choosing one
When one direction is picked and it needs a statement with one claim and its proof
When the position should come down to one word to own and an honest line to set it up
When the position starts from the product and should start from what buyers would use instead
When the position is set and each audience needs its message and proof
When you have brand facts and need key messages and proof points per audience
When the core promise needs stating: what they gain, for whom and why believe it
When you want a version with the customer as the hero, to compare with the feature-led one
When a message is true but forgettable, to test it for simple, concrete and believable
Before sign-off, to sort every claim into fine, needs proof or cut

tasks.task: Create a naming shortlist for a business or product

items.when: When a business, product, plan or range needs names created and screened with reasons
When the name and the position must be decided together for a new brand
When you want a long raw list cut to fifteen with a first clearance check
When you want name ideas from a different brief, or honest scores on names you already have
When it is a product or a rename and you want five options with why each fits
When the shortlist is ready, to score each name and get a keep, fix or drop call

tasks.task: Screen the top names before the client commits

items.when: When two to five names need checking for meaning, sound, spelling and conflicts
When a name is a favourite, to flag similar marks and risk factors before a lawyer looks
When each name needs a score and a keep, fix or drop call
When the client wants buyers, not the office, to choose between the last few names

tasks.task: Write a tagline set from different angles

items.when: When the client needs a tagline for signs, site, packaging or ads, with options and checks
Before writing, to pick the one word the line should help the brand own
When the claim is true but rivals say it too, to get fresh ways to say the same thing
When a line is right but dull, to get three versions people will repeat
When the line is for staff as much as buyers, to try two-to-four word mantras
When you have candidates, to score each on ten tests and see where it is weak
When every line is clever and none sounds like something a person would say

tasks.task: Plan a test of names, taglines or one-liners

items.when: When you have two to four options and want to know if buyers understand them
When you need a short buyer survey that shows where the brand ranks against rivals
Before the survey goes out, to remove leading questions and plan a pretest
When results are in, to find the answers that cannot be trusted

tasks.task: Set a naming system for a product range

items.when: When product, plan or feature names no longer make sense together, or a new range is coming
When there are several stores or ranges and you need a structure and a naming rule
When the client wants to put the brand name on a new product, to score how far it stretches
When the product creates a new kind of thing and the kind itself needs a plain name

tasks.task: Decide and plan a rename or message reset

items.when: When an existing brand is weighing a rename or a full message reset
Before committing, to score keep against rename and see the phases if you go ahead
When a new product needs a position, a name check and a launch with press
When the change is agreed and each channel needs its message and steps for the day
When a rename would throw away the name, colours or phrases buyers already know the brand by

tasks.task: Run the quarterly voice and message review

items.when: Every quarter, and after a big launch, a new agency or a new AI writing tool
When this quarter's live copy must be sampled and checked against the guide
When the review should also track numbers, to choose what to measure and how to collect it
Between reviews, to check each draft before it goes out

tasks.task: Write the brand story, About page or manifesto

items.when: When the founder's story should become an origin story and an About page that sound like them
When the brand stands against something and a manifesto might say it better than a story
When the draft is finished, to fix lines that sound machine-made
Before it is published, to check the piece against the voice guide and messages

tasks.task: Write the one-liner and short pitch

items.when: When the client needs 10, 30 and 60 second versions of what they do
When the pitch must be one plain line built on the word the brand owns
When the pitch only makes sense by naming a rival, to get versions that stand alone
When the one-liner will be used as a strapline, to score it on the same ten tests

tasks.task: Write up the brand strategy for sign-off

items.when: When the answers are gathered and the client wants one full strategy report
When the client is early and wants names, angles and mood directions to react to
When the report is drafted, to check purpose, voice and promises agree with each other
When the strategy must also ship as a short file writers will really open

tasks.task: Set the voice up for product copy and AI writing tools

items.when: When the guide exists and must be turned into rules a tool can follow
When you need tone, word choices and writing rules any writer or tool can apply
When buttons, errors and empty states must sound like the brand too
When the client's team writes in a shared tool and the voice should be saved in it
When the tool is set up, to test its output against the guide

always.when: When a strategy, name reason or story states a fact you cannot trace to the client or a source
Before any guide, shortlist or report goes out, to catch typos and terms spelt two ways

helpers.when: When the strategy needs a logo, colours and type, not only words
When there is no buyer evidence and interviews must be run first
When the category, its size or its rivals are not yet understood
When the new message must be written into pages that sell
When positioning is for one product launch with sales and pricing attached
When a rename or relaunch needs press

gaps: No library item writes a tagline set from several angles; only the kit prompt does
No library item checks a name for domain and social handle availability
No library item checks how a name sounds said aloud, spelt over the phone or read in other languages
No library item screens a name against registers; the first check found only flags similar marks
No library item plans a quick buyer test of names or taglines, such as a five-second or recall test
No library item sets naming rules for plans, features and versions; the one found is for stores and ranges
No library item gives clearly different voice directions to compare before the guide is written
No library item writes tone by situation, such as apology, bad news and celebration, for a service business
No library item writes a brand purpose, mission and values set for customers; those found are for staff culture
No library item runs a brand workshop with the client's team
No library item checks a positioning statement against the buyer evidence it claims to rest on
